summary: Benjamin Ide Wheeler was a linguist who studied at Brown and Heidelberg (Ph.D. under Hermann Osthoff). He held posts at Harvard, Cornell, and Berkeley, serving as Berkeley's president from 1899 to 1919.

Benjamin Lewis Rice worked in Indology and archaeology. He served as Principal of Central College of Bangalore (c. 1860–1865), Director of Public Instruction in Mysore (c. 1868–1883), and Director of the Mysore Archaeological Department (c. 1884–1889).

Benjamin Rowland was a scholar of art history, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his S.B. and Ph.D. at Harvard University. He spent his career at Harvard from 1930 to 1972 and curated Asian collections at the Fogg Art Museum.

Benjamin Schultze was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1711. He later worked as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission (1719–1726) and the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge (1728).

Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University (c. 1985–1989) and Harvard University (c. 1991–1996), and held a post at the University of Michigan around 2004.

Benjamin Wood is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Toronto under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett, and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thubten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo by 1915. He taught Buddhist studies at Shukyo, Nihon, and Waseda universities, and served as president of Taisho University and Tokai Gakuen University Junior College.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka. He served as General Editor of Gaekwad's Oriental Series and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

Benoît Vermander is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned degrees from Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute and joined Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Essers was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Amsterdam and the University of Groningen (Th.D. c. 1946–1952) under doctoral supervisor Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen.

Bernard Faure is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned doctorates from the University of Paris and Paris Diderot University. He held faculty posts at Cornell, Stanford (c. 1987–2006), and Columbia University.

Bernard Frank was a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He headed the Maison Franco-Japonaise (c. 1973–1977) and held the chair of Japanese civilization at the Collège de France from 1979 to 1996.

Bernard Goldman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan and held a post at Wayne State University from around 1956 to 1986.
Bernard Pignède was a Tibetologist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Louis Dumont from around 1956 to 1958.

Bernard S. Cohn was a scholar of South Asian history and anthropology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Cornell University (Ph.D.), later holding posts at the University of Rochester (1960–1964) and the University of Chicago (1964–1995).

Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at University College London (c. 1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (c. 1988–2003).

Bernd Barschel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Jena (Ph.D. 1976). He worked as an assistant at Halle-Wittenberg (1960–1970) and as a Lektor at Jena in 1977.
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian who held posts at the University of Oldenburg from around 1987 to 1993 and at Heidelberg University from around 2003 to 2023.

Bernfried Schlerath was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. and Habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt. He served on the faculty at Frankfurt, held a chair at Marburg, and was Professor at the Free University of Berlin (1974–1992).

Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a Ph.D. and Dr.iuris at the University of Bonn. He became a Privatdozent at Bonn in 1927 and served as Dean of faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1935.
